source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Blocking beta receptors, working in essentially the same way as a standard rescue bronchodilator medication would be expected to work","B":"Carrying fairly little established role in managing asthma that remains uncontrolled despite standard therapy already in place for the client","C":"Providing rapid rescue relief during an acute asthma attack, similar to how a short-acting bronchodilator would be expected to work","D":"Targeting specific inflammatory pathways, such as interleukin-5 (which drives eosinophil activity), offering a more targeted approach for specific asthma phenotypes"}}
source_row.rationale: Biologic medications for severe asthma, such as mepolizumab (which targets interleukin-5, a key driver of eosinophil activity), offer a more targeted approach for specific asthma phenotypes (such as eosinophilic asthma) uncontrolled on standard therapy, distinct from traditional bronchodilators and used for maintenance, not acute rescue.
source_row.source_name: PMC — Biologic Therapy Mechanisms in Severe Asthma
